explanation_english: Literally means the onset or flare-up of an illness. In Cantonese colloquial usage it often means someone suddenly starts behaving irrationally, emotionally overreacting, or having an 'episode'—similar to 'acting up' or 'having a fit'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今朝發病，發高燒，要去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 ziu1 faat3 beng6, faat3 gou1 siu1, jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天早上发病，发高烧，需要去看医生。
examples.english_sentence: He came down sick this morning with a high fever and needs to see a doctor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好又發病啦，我哋講緊正經事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jau6 faat3 beng6 laa1, ngo5 dei6 gong2 gan2 zing3 ging1 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別又发病了，我們在說正經的事。
examples.english_sentence: Don't start acting up again—we're talking about something serious.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 一講到政治佢就發病，講嘢好極端。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jat1 gong2 dou3 zing3 zi6 keoi5 zau6 faat3 beng6, gong2 je5 hou2 gik6 dyun1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 一提到政治他就发病，說話很極端。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as politics comes up he gets hysterical and says extreme things.

mandarin_meaning: 发疯、发狂
english_meaning: to go crazy / to go mad; to act irrationally; (colloquially) to go wild
explanation_mandarin: 表示失去理智或行为异常，也可用作口语，表示放纵、玩得很疯或情绪失控。
explanation_english: Indicates losing one's mind or behaving irrationally; in colloquial use can mean 'to go wild' or 'to lose control emotionally/behaviorally.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好發瘋，冷靜啲講啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 faat3 fung1, laang5 zing6 di1 gong2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要发疯，冷静点说吧。
examples.english_sentence: Don't go crazy; calm down and speak.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢考試壓力太大，快要發瘋喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haau2 si3 aat3 lik6 taai3 daai6, faai3 jiu3 faat3 fung1 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他考试压力太大，快要发疯了。
examples.english_sentence: He's under so much exam pressure he's about to go crazy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今晚去派對我哋可以盡情發瘋一晚。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 maan5 heoi3 paai3 deoi6 ngo5 dei6 ho2 ji5 zeon6 cing4 faat3 fung1 jat1 maan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今晚去派对我们可以尽情发疯一晚。
examples.english_sentence: We can let loose and go crazy at the party tonight.

mandarin_meaning: 发疯 / 发脾气 / 发飙
english_meaning: to freak out; to lose one's temper; to go crazy or act irrationally
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語/俚語，指突然情緒失控、發怒或行為失常，語氣較非正式，可形容人發瘋或暴怒的狀態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to lose control emotionally, get angry, or behave irrationally. Informal usage to describe someone 'freaking out' or 'going berserk.'

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好發瘟啦，慢慢嚟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 faat3 wan1 laa1, maan6 maan6 lai4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別發瘋了，慢慢來。
examples.english_sentence: Don't freak out, take it easy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢做錯嘢竟然發瘟，對住同事大聲喊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zou6 co3 je5 ging2 jin4 faat3 wan1, deoi3 zyu6 tung4 si6 daai6 seng1 haam3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他做錯事竟然發瘋，對著同事大聲喊。
examples.english_sentence: He made a mistake and actually freaked out, shouting loudly at his colleagues.

mandarin_meaning: 发疯／发狂（口语，用于描述行为失常或过度兴奋）
english_meaning: to go crazy / to act madly (slang); to lose one's mind or behave wildly/excessively
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話俗語，指突然失去理智或行為異常，也可指因過度興奮而表現得瘋狂或誇張，語氣可正面或負面視情境而定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning to go crazy or act madly. It can describe losing one's mind and behaving irrationally, or behaving wildly/exuberantly due to excitement; connotation depends on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日發癲，講嘢好誇張。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 faat3 din1, gong2 je5 hou2 kwaa1 zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他/她總是發瘋，說話很誇張。
examples.english_sentence: He/she is always acting crazy and speaks in a very exaggerated way.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 見到偶像，佢即刻發癲，尖叫唔停。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gin3 dou2 ngau5 zoeng6, keoi5 zik1 hak1 faat3 din1, zim1 giu3 m4 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 看到偶像，他/她立刻發瘋，尖叫不停。
examples.english_sentence: Seeing their idol, they immediately went crazy and screamed non-stop.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 尋晚球隊贏咗，班球迷喺街上發癲，跳上車慶祝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: cam4 maan5 baan1 kau4 mai4 jing4 zo2, baan1 kau4 mai4 hai2 gaai1 soeng6 faat3 din1, tiu3 soeng5 ce1 hing3 zuk1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 昨晚球隊贏了，球迷在街上瘋狂慶祝，跳上車子。
examples.english_sentence: Last night the team won; the fans went crazy in the streets, jumping on cars to celebrate.

mandarin_meaning: （口語/網絡用語）通常作為「發毛」或「發火」的變體／錯寫，表示生氣、激動或被激怒
english_meaning: Colloquial/Internet variant (often a misspelling) of expressions like 'get riled up' or 'lose one's temper' — to become angry, upset, or provoked
explanation_mandarin: 「發矛」多見於口語或網絡語境，常被當作「發毛」或「發火」的變體或錯寫，用來形容突然變得激動、生氣或被挑釁而反應強烈。此詞並非標準書面詞彙，屬俗語/網絡用語。
explanation_english: “發矛” appears mainly in spoken Cantonese or online contexts and is often used as a variant or misspelling of terms like '發毛' or '發火'. It describes becoming agitated, angry, or reacting strongly when provoked. It is colloquial and not standard formal vocabulary.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一聽到嗰件事就開始發矛，講嘢好激動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 teng1 dou3 go2 gin6 si6 zau6 hoi1 ci2 faat3 maau4, gong2 je5 hou2 gik1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一听到那件事就开始發矛，说话很激动。
examples.english_sentence: He started getting worked up when he heard about it; he spoke very emotionally.

mandarin_meaning: （罕用）生成硝石；硝化（指鹽類或硝鹽在材料或土壤上沉積或出現）
english_meaning: rare/technical: to produce saltpetre (niter); to undergo nitrification or saltpetre deposition
explanation_mandarin: 「發硝」屬罕見或較技術性的用法，字面意思為產生硝石（俗稱「硝」或「硝鹽」）。常用於描述建材、牆面、土壤等在含鹽環境下出現白色鹽類結晶或硝鹽沉積的現象。現代口語廣泛使用較少，常見替代詞有「硝化」「產硝」等。
explanation_english: “發硝” is a rare/technical Cantonese term meaning to produce saltpetre (niter) or to undergo nitrification/salt deposition. It is used to describe the appearance of white salt crystals or nitrate deposits on materials such as walls, timber, or soil in saline conditions. It is not common in everyday speech; terms like “硝化” or “produce saltpetre” are more typical in technical contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲土壤長年暴露喺鹽分高嘅環境，可能會發硝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 tou2 joeng5 coeng4 nin4 bou6 lou6 hai2 jim4 fan6 gou1 ge3 waan4 ging2, ho2 nang4 wui5 faat3 siu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那片土壤長期暴露在高鹽環境中，可能會發硝。
examples.english_sentence: That soil, after long exposure to a high-salt environment, may develop saltpetre.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）發瘋、行為或言語失常、情緒失控
english_meaning: to act crazy; to behave irrationally or erratically; to lose one's mind (colloquial/slang)
explanation_mandarin: 口語用語，表示突然行為怪異、言語無理或情緒失控，常用來批評或描述某人行為不正常。
explanation_english: A colloquial/slang expression meaning to act irrationally, crazily, or erratically — to lose one's composure or behave in a very unreasonable way.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日發神經，成日亂講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1jat6 faat3 san4 ging1, sing4 jat6 lyun6 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天發神經，老是亂說話。
examples.english_sentence: He's acting crazy today, keeps saying nonsense.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好喺公眾場合發神經，好尷尬。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 hai2 gung1 zung3 coeng4 hap6 faat3 san4 ging1, hou2 gaam1 ngaak3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要在公共場合發神經，會很尷尬。
examples.english_sentence: Don't go crazy in public; it'll be embarrassing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔係發神經，只係唔想理你啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 hai6 faat3 san4 ging1, zi2 hai6 m4 soeng2 lei5 nei5 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不是發神經，只是不想理你而已。
examples.english_sentence: I'm not going crazy; I just don't want to bother with you.

mandarin_meaning: 发祥地
english_meaning: place of origin; birthplace (of a culture, tradition, movement, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 指某種文化、宗教、行業、民族或事物最初出現、發展或興起的地點。
explanation_english: Refers to the location where a culture, religion, industry, clan, or other phenomenon first appeared, developed, or originated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 梅州被視為客家文化嘅發祥地。
examples.jyutping_sentence: mui4 zau1 bei6 si6 wai4 hak3 gaa1 man4 faa3 ge3 faat3 coeng4 dei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 梅州被视为客家文化的发祥地。
examples.english_sentence: Meizhou is regarded as the birthplace of Hakka culture.

mandarin_meaning: 发票
english_meaning: invoice; receipt
explanation_mandarin: 用於記錄交易或付款的票據，可作為報銷或報稅的憑證；在日常語境中也常指商店給予的收據。
explanation_english: A paper or electronic document issued to record a sale or payment; can serve as proof for reimbursement or tax purposes. In everyday usage it often refers to the receipt given by a shop.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 買嘢記得索取發票，返公司可以報銷。
examples.jyutping_sentence: maai5 je5 gei3 dak1 sok3 ceot1 faat3 piu3, faan1 gung1 si1 ho2 ji5 bou3 siu1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 买东西记得索取发票，回公司可以报销。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to ask for a receipt when you buy something — you can use it for reimbursement at the office.

mandarin_meaning: 发福（長肉、變胖）
english_meaning: to gain weight; to become plumper; put on weight (often used euphemistically to suggest looking healthier or more prosperous)
explanation_mandarin: 「發福」指身體變得圓潤或長肉，通常用來形容發胖，有時帶有生活富足、看起來健康或有福氣的婉轉含義。
explanation_english: Refers to becoming plumper or gaining weight. Often used to describe someone who looks fuller or healthier from weight gain; can be a euphemistic or mildly complimentary way to say someone has put on weight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你最近發福咗喎，係咪食多咗？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 zeoi3 gan6 faat3 fuk1 zo2 wo3, hai6 mai6 sik6 do1 zo2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你最近發福了，是不是吃得比較多？
examples.english_sentence: You've been putting on weight recently — have you been eating more?

mandarin_meaning: 发稿；发布新闻稿或把稿件提交给编辑/媒体
english_meaning: to issue/send out a press release or submit an article/manuscript to editors/media
explanation_mandarin: 在新聞、媒體或公司語境中，指發佈新聞稿、將稿件提交給編輯或媒體，或者把稿件發出以供發布。
explanation_english: In journalism, media, or corporate contexts, it means issuing a press release or submitting/sending a manuscript or article to editors or the media for publication.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 記者已經發稿喇，等緊編輯覆核。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gei3 ze2 ji5 ging1 faat3 gou2 laa3, dang2 gan2 bin1 zaap6 fuk1 hat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 記者已經發稿了，等編輯復核。
examples.english_sentence: The reporter has already submitted the article; waiting for the editor to review it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司打算聽日發稿，宣佈新產品。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 daa2 syun3 ting1 jat6 faat3 gou2, syun1 bou3 san1 caan2 ban2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司打算明天發稿，宣布新產品。
examples.english_sentence: The company plans to issue the press release tomorrow to announce the new product.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我仲未發稿，因為相片未整理好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zung6 mei6 faat3 gou2, jan1 wai6 soeng2 pin3 mei6 zing2 lei5 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我還沒發稿，因為照片還沒整理好。
examples.english_sentence: I haven't sent the article yet because the photos aren't organized.

mandarin_meaning: （口語/俚語）因窮或受挫而變得小氣、刻薄或易發脾氣
english_meaning: slang: to become petty, mean, or short-tempered (often because of poverty or frustration)
explanation_mandarin: 「發窮惡」是廣東話俗語，形容一個人因為經濟困難或受挫而變得小器、刻薄或容易發脾氣，對人態度差。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase describing someone who, often due to poverty or frustration, becomes petty, mean, or short-tempered toward others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢最近失業，開始發窮惡，對人又唔客氣又小氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 zeoi3 gan6 sat1 jip6, hoi1 ci2 faat3 kung4 ngok6, deoi3 jan4 jau6 m4 haak3 hei3 jau6 siu2 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他最近失業，開始發窮惡，對人既不客氣又小氣。
examples.english_sentence: He recently lost his job and started acting stingy and short-tempered toward others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好因為錢唔夠就發窮惡，咁樣會得罪人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 jan1 wai6 cin2 m4 gau3 zau6 faat3 kung4 ngok6, gam2 joeng6 wui5 dak1 zeoi6 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要因為錢不夠就發窮惡，這樣會得罪人。
examples.english_sentence: Don't start acting petty because you don't have enough money; that will offend people.

mandarin_meaning: 发笑
english_meaning: to laugh; to burst into laughter; to find something laughable
explanation_mandarin: 表示發出笑聲，常用於表達覺得可笑、忍不住笑或帶有嘲笑意味的反應。
explanation_english: To laugh or burst into laughter; used to indicate finding something funny, being unable to hold back laughter, or sometimes to ridicule someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢講嘅笑話好冷，我都忍唔住發笑。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gong2 ge3 siu3waa6 hou2 laang5, ngo5 dou1 jan2 m4 zyu6 faat3 siu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他讲的笑话很冷，我都忍不住发笑。
examples.english_sentence: His joke was so corny that I couldn't help laughing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好發笑佢，佢真係唔識。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 faat3 siu3 keoi5, keoi5 zan1 hai6 m4 sik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要嘲笑他，他真的不懂。
examples.english_sentence: Don't laugh at him; he really doesn't understand.

mandarin_meaning: 發粉（泡打粉、發酵粉等膨鬆劑）
english_meaning: baking powder / leavening agent
explanation_mandarin: 指用於烘焙或製作糕點，使麵糰或麵糊膨鬆的粉狀物（如泡打粉、發酵粉）。在廣東話中常用來稱呼這類膨鬆劑。
explanation_english: Refers to powdery leavening agents (such as baking powder) used in baking and pastry-making to make doughs or batters rise. In Cantonese it commonly denotes these raising agents.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 整蛋糕記得落啲發粉，先會鬆軟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing2 daan6 gou1 gei3 dak1 lok6 di1 faat3 fan2, sin1 wui5 sung1 jyun5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 做蛋糕記得放一些發粉，這樣才會鬆軟。
examples.english_sentence: Remember to add some baking powder when making the cake so it will be fluffy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢袋發粉係買嚟整糕點用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 doi2 faat3 fan2 hai6 maai5 lai4 zing2 gou1 dim2 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這袋發粉是買來做糕點用的。
examples.english_sentence: This bag of baking powder was bought for making pastries.

mandarin_meaning: （臉或皮膚）變紫；因憤怒臉色發紫；或指瘀青變紫
english_meaning: to turn purple (face or skin); to look purple from anger; to bruise and become purple
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，常用來形容因為很生氣而臉色發紫，或指身體部位瘀傷變紫。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial phrase describing someone whose face or skin turns purple — commonly from extreme anger — or a body part that has bruised and become purple.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢氣到面都發紫，連句說話都講唔出。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hei3 dou3 min6 dou1 faat3 zi2, lin4 geoi3 syut3 waa6 dou1 gong2 m4 ceot1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他氣得臉都發紫，連一句話都說不出來。
examples.english_sentence: He was so angry his face turned purple; he couldn't even say a word.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢跌親隻腳，腫到發紫要去睇醫生。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dit3 can1 zek3 goek3, zung2 dou3 faat3 zi2 jiu3 heoi3 tai2 ji1 sang1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他跌傷了腳，腫得發紫要去看醫生。
examples.english_sentence: He injured his foot in a fall; it was swollen and turned purple and he had to see a doctor.

mandarin_meaning: 手淫；打飛機（粗俗）
english_meaning: to masturbate (male); jerk off (vulgar)
explanation_mandarin: 香港俗語、粗口，用來指男性手淫或打飛機，有時也用來形容性衝動。屬於粗俗、冒犯性的表達。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong vulgar slang term referring to male masturbation (to jerk off). It can also be used to describe someone being sexually aroused. Considered crude and offensive.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺度發羊吊，啲細路會睇到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dou6 faat3 joeng4 diu3, di1 sai3 lou6 wui5 tai2 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要在這裡手淫，孩子會看到。
examples.english_sentence: Don't masturbate here, the kids might see.

mandarin_meaning: 发脾气／发火／生气
english_meaning: to lose one's temper; to get angry; to fly into a tantrum
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語，指突然或常常發脾氣、生氣或耍性子（有時針對小事）。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression meaning to lose one's temper, get angry, or throw a tantrum (sometimes over small matters).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日發老脾，大家都唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 faat3 lou5 pei4, daai6 gaa1 dou1 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要总是发脾气，大家都不高兴。
examples.english_sentence: Don't always lose your temper; nobody is happy about it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一遲到就發老脾，真煩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 ci4 dou3 zau6 faat3 lou5 pei4, zan1 faan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一迟到就发脾气，真烦。
examples.english_sentence: He gets angry as soon as he's late — it's really annoying.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 小朋友發老脾係好正常，父母要冷靜處理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: siu2 pang4 jau5 faat3 lou5 pei4 hai6 hou2 zing3 soeng4, fu6 mou5 jiu3 laang5 zing6 cyu2 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 小孩子发脾气是很正常，父母要冷静处理。
examples.english_sentence: It's normal for children to throw tantrums; parents should handle it calmly.

mandarin_meaning: 发声 / 发表声明、表态
english_meaning: to make a sound; to speak up; to issue a statement
explanation_mandarin: 表示發出聲音或公開表態、發表聲明，既可指實際出聲，也可指單位或個人發佈聲明。
explanation_english: To produce a sound or to voice an opinion; can mean physically making a sound or publicly issuing a statement on an issue.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府仲未就呢件事發聲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 zung6 mei6 zau6 ni1 gin6 si6 faat3 seng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府還未就這件事發表聲明。
examples.english_sentence: The government has not yet issued a statement about this matter.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好淨係喺網上發聲，試下親自同佢哋傾下。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 mong5 soeng6 faat3 seng1, si3 haa5 can1 zi6 tung4 keoi5 dei6 king1 haa5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要只在網上發聲，試著親自和他們談談。
examples.english_sentence: Don't just voice opinions online; try talking to them in person.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司今日發聲，澄清嗰個傳聞。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gam1 jat6 faat3 seng1, cing4 cing1 go2 go3 cyun4 man4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司今天發表聲明，澄清那個傳聞。
examples.english_sentence: The company issued a statement today to clarify that rumor.

mandarin_meaning: 发育 (生长、发达、发育)
english_meaning: to develop; (physical) growth; development
partOfSpeech_english: verb (can also be used as a noun: development)
explanation_mandarin: 指生物體（尤其是兒童或青少年）在身體器官、組織或生理功能上的生長與成熟過程；也可泛指其他方面的發展。
explanation_english: Refers to the biological process of growth and maturation of an organism's organs, tissues, or physiological functions (especially in children and adolescents); can also more generally mean development or growth.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個細路發育得好快，身高同體重都多咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 sai3 lou6 faat3 juk6 dak1 hou2 faai3, san1 gou1 tung4 tai2 zung6 dou1 do1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个小孩发育得很快，身高和体重都增加了。
examples.english_sentence: The child is developing quickly; both height and weight have increased.

mandarin_meaning: 发胖 / 变胖（体重增加）
english_meaning: to gain weight; to become fat
explanation_mandarin: 指体重增加或身体变得比以前更胖。
explanation_english: Refers to gaining weight or becoming physically fatter than before.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 最近食得多，發胖咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zeoi3 gan6 sik6 dak1 do1, faat3 pun3 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 最近吃得多，发胖了。
examples.english_sentence: I've been eating a lot recently and have gained weight.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢因為冇運動，開始發胖。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1 wai6 mou5 wan6 dung6, hoi1 ci2 faat3 pun3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他因为没运动，开始发胖。
examples.english_sentence: He started to gain weight because he hasn't been exercising.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好驚發胖，要均衡飲食先健康。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 geng1 faat3 pun3, jiu3 gwan1 hang4 jam2 sik6 sin1 gin6 hong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要怕发胖，要均衡饮食才健康。
examples.english_sentence: Don't be afraid of gaining weight; balanced eating is what keeps you healthy.

mandarin_meaning: 发胀；肿胀
english_meaning: to swell; to become bloated or inflated
explanation_mandarin: 指器官、身体部位或物体因积液、气体、压力等原因而鼓起、变大或肿起。
explanation_english: Refers to a body part or object becoming swollen or enlarged due to fluid, gas, pressure, or other causes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我隻手發脹，可能係俾蚊咬到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zek3 sau2 faat3 zoeng3, ho2 nang4 hai6 bei2 man1 ngaau5 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我的手发胀，可能是被蚊子咬了。
examples.english_sentence: My hand is swollen; it might have been bitten by a mosquito.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個氣球吹太多口，開始發脹，應該唔好再吹。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 hei3 kau4 ceoi1 taai3 do1 hau2, hoi1 ci2 faat3 zoeng3, jing1 goi1 m4 hou2 zoi3 ceoi1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 气球吹太多，开始膨胀，不应该再吹。
examples.english_sentence: The balloon was blown too much and started to swell; you shouldn't blow it more.

mandarin_meaning: 发脾气
english_meaning: to lose one's temper; to get angry; to throw a tantrum
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，源自「發脾氣」的諧音變體，用法口語化，帶有輕微戲謔或誇張色彩，表示生氣或發脾氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang variant of "發脾氣" (to lose one's temper). It's an informal, often joking or exaggerated way to say someone is getting angry or throwing a tantrum.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁樣講我就想發脾四喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 joeng6 gong2 ngo5 zau6 soeng2 faat3 pei4 sei3 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你這樣說我就想發脾氣了。
examples.english_sentence: If you say that, I feel like losing my temper.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢考唔到分就發脾四，真係太誇張。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 haau2 m4 dou2 fan1 zau6 faat3 pei4 sei3, zan1 hai6 taai3 kwaa1 zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他考不到分就發脾氣，真的是太誇張。
examples.english_sentence: He gets angry when he doesn't get marks — it's really over the top.

mandarin_meaning: 发脾气；生气、发怒
english_meaning: to lose one's temper; to get angry; to throw a tantrum
explanation_mandarin: 表示生气、发怒，失去冷静。可以指成年人或小孩因不满或挫折而表现出抱怨、大声或哭闹。
explanation_english: To become angry or lose one's temper — to react angrily or sulk because of annoyance, dissatisfaction, or frustration.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好成日對住細路仔發脾氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 deoi3 zyu6 sai3 lou6 zai2 faat3 pei4 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要老是对着小孩子发脾气。
examples.english_sentence: Don't keep losing your temper with the kids.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢因為考試唔好，發咗脾氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1 wai6 haau2 si3 m4 hou2, faat3 zo2 pei4 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他因为考试不及格而发脾气。
examples.english_sentence: He got angry because he did poorly on the exam.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 同事一早就遲到，老闆發脾氣啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: tung4 si6 jat1 zou2 zau6 ci4 dou3, lou5 baan2 faat3 pei4 hei3 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 同事一早就迟到，老板发脾气了。
examples.english_sentence: A colleague was late first thing this morning, and the boss lost his temper.

mandarin_meaning: 出脚；踢人；用脚攻击（常用于武术或打斗场合）
english_meaning: to kick; to strike with the foot; to launch a kick (often in martial arts or a physical altercation)
explanation_mandarin: 「發腳」是廣東話的動詞，指用腳發力踢出攻擊或動作，常見於武術、打鬥或形容用腳反擊的情況。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, '發腳' (faat3 goek3) is a verb meaning to deliver a kick or strike with the foot. It's commonly used in martial arts, fights, or to describe kicking as a form of physical response.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 兩個打交嗰陣，佢第一時間就發腳反擊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: loeng5 go3 daa2 gaau1 go2 zan6, keoi5 dai6 jat1 si4 gaan3 zau6 faat3 goek3 faan2 gik1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 两个打架的时候，他第一时间就出脚反击。
examples.english_sentence: When the two were fighting, he immediately kicked back.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 做武術要練好發腳，唔好淨係練手技。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zou6 mou5 seot6 jiu3 lin6 hou2 faat3 goek3, m4 hou2 zing6 hai6 lin6 sau2 gei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 练武术要练好发脚，不要只练手法。
examples.english_sentence: In martial arts you should practice your kicking technique, not only hand techniques.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見人講大話忍唔住，氣到想發腳。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 jan4 gong2 daai6 waa6 jan2 m4 zyu6, hei3 dou3 soeng2 faat3 goek3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到别人说谎忍不住，气得想出脚（踢人）。
examples.english_sentence: He couldn't stand the lies and was so angry he wanted to kick (someone).

mandarin_meaning: 发自（来源于，出自）
english_meaning: to come from; to originate from (often used to indicate feelings or intentions originating from the heart or sincerity)
explanation_mandarin: 表示某種情感、想法或行為來源於某處或某人，常見搭配如「發自內心／發自真心」，表示出自真心或真誠。
explanation_english: Indicates that a feeling, thought, or action originates from somewhere or someone. Commonly used in phrases like '發自內心' (from the heart) or '發自真心' (sincerely).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢嘅笑容發自內心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 ge3 siu3 jung4 faat3 zi6 noi6 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他的笑容发自内心。
examples.english_sentence: His smile comes from the heart.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢發自真心幫助我。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faat3 zi6 zan1 sam1 bong1 zo6 ngo5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他发自真心地帮助我。
examples.english_sentence: He helped me sincerely / from the heart.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢句說話係發自內心，唔係敷衍。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 geoi3 syut3 waa6 hai6 faat3 zi6 noi6 sam1, m4 hai6 fuk1 jin5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这句话是发自内心的，不是敷衍。
examples.english_sentence: This sentence is from the heart, not perfunctory.

mandarin_meaning: 發出臭味；變臭；（口語）耍脾氣、發脾氣
english_meaning: to give off a foul smell; to go bad; (colloquial) to sulk or throw a tantrum
explanation_mandarin: 「發臭」可指物品變壞、散發難聞氣味；口語中也可用來形容人耍脾氣、擺臭面。
explanation_english: “發臭” can mean that something has gone bad and emits a bad smell; colloquially it can also describe someone sulking or showing a bad temper.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢塊豬肉放咗太耐，已經發臭，唔可以食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 faai3 zyu1 juk6 fong3 zo2 taai3 noi6, ji5 ging1 faat3 cau3, m4 ho2 ji5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這塊豬肉放太久，已經發臭，不能吃。
examples.english_sentence: This piece of pork was left too long and has gone bad; it can't be eaten.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好發臭啦，有咩事就講啦，我哋幫你搵辦法。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 faat3 cau3 laa1, jau5 me1 si6 zau6 gong2 laa1, ngo5 dei6 bong1 nei5 wan2 baan6 faat3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別耍脾氣，有事就說，我們幫你想辦法。
examples.english_sentence: Don't sulk. If there's something wrong, tell us and we'll help you find a solution.

mandarin_meaning: 发花痴 / 發花癡（对喜欢的人或偶像表现出痴迷、发傻的样子）
english_meaning: to go gaga/act lovestruck; to become infatuated and act silly over someone
explanation_mandarin: 指看到喜欢的人或偶像时表现出痴迷、出神或做出傻样，带有调侃或俚语色彩。
explanation_english: Refers to behaving lovestruck or gaga when seeing someone you like or an idol, often acting silly or overly infatuated; informal/slangy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到男神會發花痴，整個人都傻咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 naam4 san4 wui5 faat3 faa1 ci1, zing2 go3 jan4 dou1 so4 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 她看到男神就發花癡，整個人都傻了。
examples.english_sentence: She goes gaga when she sees her crush; she becomes totally silly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲粉絲喺演唱會度不停發花痴，尖叫聲好大。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 fan2 si1 hai2 jin2 coeng3 wui2 dou6 bat1 ting4 faat3 faa1 ci1, zim1 giu3 seng1 hou2 daai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 粉絲在演唱會上不停地發花癡，尖叫聲很大。
examples.english_sentence: The fans kept going gaga at the concert, screaming loudly.

mandarin_meaning: 发疯；发神经；胡闹
english_meaning: to go crazy; to act erratically or wildly (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粤语口语用语，表示突然行为异常、发疯或胡闹，有时带开玩笑的语气，也可指精神失常。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to go crazy, act erratically or wildly. Can be used jokingly or to indicate someone losing their mind.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好發花癲，冷靜啲啦！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 faat3 faa1 din1, laang5 zing6 di1 laa1!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要发神经，冷静点！
examples.english_sentence: Don't go crazy; calm down!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽到嗰個消息即刻發花癲，成個人好興奮。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 dou3 go2 go3 siu1 sik1 zik1 hak1 faat3 faa1 din1, seng4 go3 jan4 hou2 hing1 fan5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他听到那个消息立刻发疯了，整个人很兴奋。
examples.english_sentence: When he heard the news he immediately went nuts — he was totally excited.

mandarin_meaning: 发芽（开始长出芽）
english_meaning: to sprout; to germinate; (figuratively) to begin to emerge or develop
explanation_mandarin: 指植物的種子或芽開始長出胚芽；引申為某種想法、興趣或潮流開始出現或萌生。
explanation_english: Refers to seeds or plants beginning to produce shoots; figuratively, it means ideas, interests, or trends starting to emerge or develop.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢啲種子已經開始發芽喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 di1 zung2 zi2 ji5 ging1 hoi1 ci2 faat3 ngaa4 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这些种子已经开始发芽了。
examples.english_sentence: These seeds have started to sprout.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢對攝影嘅興趣慢慢發芽，之後變得好投入。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 deoi3 sip3 jing2 ge3 hing3 ceoi3 maan6 maan6 faat3 ngaa4, zi1 hau6 bin3 dak1 hou2 tau6 jap6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他對攝影的興趣慢慢萌芽，之後變得很投入。
examples.english_sentence: His interest in photography slowly took root and later became very involved.

mandarin_meaning: 受驚；驚慌（粵語口語）；有時亦指情緒激動、生氣
english_meaning: to get scared/spooked or to become startled; colloquially can also mean to get upset/angry
explanation_mandarin: 「發茅」為粵語俗語，常用來形容見到可怕或突發情況而受驚、慌張、緊張的反應。有時在口語中亦可指情緒激動或發怒。字形常與「發毛」互用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to be frightened, startled, or panicked by something. In casual speech it can also be used to describe becoming agitated or angry. Often written or pronounced interchangeably with "發毛".

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到老鼠即刻發茅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 lou5 syu2 zik1 haak1 faat3 mou4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到老鼠就立刻受驚。
examples.english_sentence: He got scared as soon as he saw the mouse.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好咁發茅，我只係開個玩笑啫。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 faat3 mou4, ngo5 zi2 hai6 hoi1 go3 waan6 siu3 ze1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你別這樣生氣/緊張，我只是在開玩笑而已。
examples.english_sentence: Don't get so worked up; I was only joking.

mandarin_meaning: 安排；交代去做某事；處理、處置（口語）
english_meaning: to assign or instruct someone to do something; to arrange or handle; (colloquially) to deal with or punish someone
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，表示把事情分派、安排行動或交代他人去處理；在某些語境亦可指處置或懲罰某人。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese verb meaning to assign, arrange, or instruct someone to handle a task; in some contexts it can also mean to deal with or punish someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你發落佢去準備會議資料啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 faat3 lok6 keoi5 heoi3 zeon2 bei6 wui6 ji5 zi1 liu2 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你交代他去準備會議資料吧。
examples.english_sentence: You assign him to prepare the meeting materials.

mandarin_meaning: 发号施令；下达命令、发布指示
english_meaning: to issue orders; to give commands; to boss people around
explanation_mandarin: 表示下达命令或发出指示，通常用于形容有权力者对他人发出命令。有时带有贬义，暗示只会发号而不亲自做事或专横指挥。
explanation_english: Means to issue orders or give directives, often used to describe someone in authority commanding others. It can carry a negative connotation implying bossiness or doing only the ordering rather than the work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日淨係識發號施令，自己唔做嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 zing6 hai6 sik1 faat3 hou6 si1 ling6, zi6 gei2 m4 zou6 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是只会发号施令，自己不做事。
examples.english_sentence: He always just issues orders and doesn't do any work himself.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上司喺會議入面成日發號施令，員工覺得好唔開心。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 si1 hai2 wui6 ji5 jap6 min6 sing4 jat6 faat3 hou6 si1 ling6, jyun4 gung1 gok3 dak1 hou2 m4 hoi1 sam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 上司在会议里总是发号施令，员工感到很不开心。
examples.english_sentence: The boss is always issuing orders in meetings, and the employees feel very unhappy.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府喺緊急情況下可能會發號施令，限制公眾活動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 hai2 gan2 gap1 cing4 fong3 haa6 ho2 nang4 wui5 faat3 hou6 si1 ling6, haan6 zai3 gung1 zung3 wut6 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府在紧急情况下可能会发号施令，限制公众活动。
examples.english_sentence: The government may issue directives during an emergency, restricting public activities.

mandarin_meaning: 發瘋；發癲；情緒失控（口語）
english_meaning: to freak out; to go crazy; to lose one's temper (colloquial)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語俚語，用來形容一個人情緒失控、發脾氣或行為怪異，意思接近「發癲／發瘋」。多在非正式語境或香港口語中使用。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang verb meaning to lose control emotionally, freak out, or act crazily — similar to '發癲/發瘋' in Mandarin. Used in informal Hong Kong Cantonese.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢畀老闆罵嘅時候，差啲發蛋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 bei2 lou5 baan2 maa6 ge3 si4 hau6, caa1 di1 faat3 daan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他被老闆罵的時候，差點發瘋。
examples.english_sentence: When he was scolded by his boss, he nearly freaked out.

mandarin_meaning: 发行 (fāxíng)
english_meaning: to issue; to publish; to circulate
explanation_mandarin: 表示发售、发布或使流通，例如发行股票、发行货币、发行书籍等。
explanation_english: Means to issue, publish, or circulate something — for example issuing shares, currency, books, or other publications.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢本書已經發行咗三個月。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 bun2 syu1 ji5 ging1 faat3 hang4 zo2 saam1 go3 jyut6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这本书已经发行了三个月。
examples.english_sentence: This book has been published (issued) for three months.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司計劃下星期發行新嘅股票。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 gai3 waak6 haa6 sing1 kei4 faat3 hang4 san1 ge3 gu2 piu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司计划下星期发行新的股票。
examples.english_sentence: The company plans to issue new shares next week.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 中央銀行打算發行新紙幣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zung1 joeng1 ngan4 hong4 daa2 syun3 faat3 hang4 san1 zi2 bai6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 中央银行打算发行新纸币。
examples.english_sentence: The central bank plans to issue new banknotes.

mandarin_meaning: 发表（fābiǎo）——发布、公布；发表意见或学术成果
english_meaning: to publish; to issue; to announce; to express (an opinion); to present (a paper)
explanation_mandarin: 表示把某項意見、文章、研究成果或聲明向公眾或特定場合公開說出或發布。
explanation_english: To make something public or formally present it — e.g., publish an article, announce a statement, or express an opinion at a meeting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺會議上發表咗意見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 wui6 ji5 soeng6 faat3 biu2 zo2 ji3 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在会议上发表了意见。
examples.english_sentence: He expressed his opinion at the meeting.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢篇論文已經發表喺國際期刊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 pin1 leon6 man4 ji5 ging1 faat3 biu2 hai2 gwok3 zai3 kei4 hon1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这篇论文已经发表在国际期刊上。
examples.english_sentence: This paper has been published in an international journal.

mandarin_meaning: 發覺 (fājué) — 意識到、察覺、發現
english_meaning: to realize; to notice; to become aware of
explanation_mandarin: 表示突然或經過觀察後意識到某件事、發現某情況，常用於表達察覺到某種變化或問題。
explanation_english: Indicates becoming aware of or noticing something (often suddenly or after observation); used to express discovering a situation, change, or problem.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我啱啱先發覺自己拎錯咗袋。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 aam1 aam1 sin1 faat3 gok3 zi6 gei2 ling1 co3 zo2 doi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我剛剛發覺我拿錯了袋子。
examples.english_sentence: I just realized I grabbed the wrong bag.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢突然發覺自己唔鍾意呢份工。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dat6 jin4 faat3 gok3 zi6 gei2 m4 zung1 ji3 ni1 fan6 gung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他突然發覺自己不喜歡這份工作。
examples.english_sentence: He suddenly realized he didn't like this job.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你有冇發覺今朝凍咗？
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 jau5 mou5 faat3 gok3 gam1 ziu1 dung3 zo2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你有沒有發覺今天早上變冷了？
examples.english_sentence: Did you notice it got colder this morning?

mandarin_meaning: 发言（fāyán）：发表意见、说话；在会议或场合中发言
english_meaning: to speak; to make a statement; speech or the act of speaking (e.g., at a meeting)
explanation_mandarin: “發言”可作动词，表示说话或发表意见；也可作名词，指在会议、讨论等场合的发言行为或发言权。
explanation_english: “發言” can be a verb meaning to speak or express an opinion, or a noun referring to the act or right of speaking (often used in meetings, panels, or discussions).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你可以發言㗎，講出你嘅意見。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 ho2 ji5 faat3 jin4 gaa3, gong2 ceot1 nei5 ge3 ji3 gin3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你可以发言，讲出你的意见。
examples.english_sentence: You can speak up and express your opinion.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 主持人叫每個嘉賓逐一發言。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zyu2 ci4 jan4 giu3 mui5 go3 gaa1 ban1 zuk6 jat1 faat3 jin4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 主持人叫每个嘉宾逐一发言。
examples.english_sentence: The host asked each guest to speak in turn.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺會議上發言好有條理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 wui6 ji5 soeng6 faat3 jin4 hou2 jau5 tiu4 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在会议上发言很有条理。
examples.english_sentence: He spoke very coherently at the meeting.

mandarin_meaning: 发言人（代表機構或團體對外發言的人）
english_meaning: spokesperson; a person who speaks on behalf of an organization or group
explanation_mandarin: 指代表某個機構、組織或團體對外發表聲明、回應媒體或處理公眾查詢的人。
explanation_english: A person appointed to speak on behalf of an organization or group, issuing statements and responding to media or public enquiries.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 政府今日任命咗新嘅發言人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: zing3 fu2 gam1 jat6 jam6 ming6 zo2 san1 ge3 faat3 jin4 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 政府今天任命了新的发言人。
examples.english_sentence: The government appointed a new spokesperson today.

mandarin_meaning: 发誓
english_meaning: to swear; to vow; to make a solemn promise
explanation_mandarin: 表示郑重地作出承诺或宣誓，通常用来保证某事是真的或将会去做某事。
explanation_english: To make a solemn promise or oath; to assert seriously that something is true or that one will do something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我發誓我冇講過嗰件事。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 faat3 si3 ngo5 mou5 gong2 gwo3 go2 gin6 si6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我发誓我没有说过那件事。
examples.english_sentence: I swear I didn't say that.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢向我發誓以後唔會遲到。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoeng3 ngo5 faat3 si3 ji5 hau6 m4 wui5 ci4 dou3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他向我发誓以后不会迟到。
examples.english_sentence: He swore to me he wouldn't be late again.

jyutping: faat3 seoi3 dong3 sik6 saang1 coi3
mandarin_meaning: （粵語口語）發誓時用來強調誠意或帶有諷刺意味的說法，字面意思是「發誓的話就去吃生菜」，暗指若不守承諾就甘願承受羞辱或懲罰。
english_meaning: A Cantonese colloquial expression used to emphasize a vow or used sarcastically. Literally "swear and (I'll) eat raw lettuce," implying willingness to do something unpleasant (or be humiliated) if the promise is broken.
explanation_mandarin: 此短語多用於日常口語，說話者用來強調自己說話的誠意或以誇張方式表示如果不守承諾就會接受尷尬或懲罰。也可用作諷刺，表示不相信對方的話。
explanation_english: Used in everyday Cantonese to stress the speaker's sincerity or, jokingly/exaggeratedly, to state that they'd accept embarrassment or punishment if they break the promise. It can also be used sarcastically to show disbelief in someone else's claim.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我發誓當食生菜，我真係唔會再遲到！
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 faat3 seoi3 dong3 sik6 saang1 coi3, ngo5 zan1 hai6 m4 wui5 zoi3 ci4 dou3!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我發誓（真的），我不會再遲到！
examples.english_sentence: I swear — I'll eat raw lettuce if I'm lying, I really won't be late again!

mandarin_meaning: 发财 (fā cái)
english_meaning: to get rich; to become wealthy; to make a fortune
explanation_mandarin: 表示獲得大量錢財或變得富有。常用作祝賀語（如農曆新年時說「恭喜發財」），亦可作口語動詞使用。
explanation_english: Means to become wealthy or to make a fortune. Commonly used as a greeting/blessing (e.g. during Lunar New Year: "Gong hei fat choy"), and also used as a verbal expression in everyday speech.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年快樂，恭喜發財！
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 faai3 lok6, gung1 hei2 faat3 coi4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新年快乐，恭喜发财！
examples.english_sentence: Happy New Year — wishing you prosperity!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢希望開公司之後可以好快發財。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hei1 mong6 hoi1 gung1 si1 zi1 hau6 ho2 ji5 hou2 faai3 faat3 coi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他希望开公司之后可以很快发财。
examples.english_sentence: He hopes that after starting the company he can get rich quickly.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢賭咗一大注，諗住今次會發財。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dou2 zo2 jat1 daai6 zyu3, lam2 zyu6 gam1 ci3 wui5 faat3 coi4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他赌了一大注，想着这次会发财。
examples.english_sentence: He placed a big bet, thinking he'd get rich this time.

mandarin_meaning: 祝願發財、買賣興旺（祝賀語）
english_meaning: A greeting wishing someone wealth and prosperous business
explanation_mandarin: 粵語的祝賀用語，常在農曆新年、開業或拜年時使用，意思是祝願對方發財、買賣興旺、好運連連。
explanation_english: A Cantonese greeting used to wish someone wealth and brisk business. Commonly used during Lunar New Year, shop openings, or when congratulating someone on business-related occasions.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年快樂，發財好市！
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 faai3 lok6, faat3 coi4 hou2 si5!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新年快樂，祝你發財，生意興隆！
examples.english_sentence: Happy New Year — wishing you wealth and prosperous business!

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你今日開鋪？我祝你發財好市，生意興隆！
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam1 jat6 hoi1 pou3? ngo5 zuk1 nei5 faat3 coi4 hou2 si5, saang1 ji3 hing1 lung4!
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你今天開店嗎？我祝你發財，生意興隆！
examples.english_sentence: Are you opening your shop today? I wish you wealth and booming business!

mandarin_meaning: 想快速發財的人（俚語）
english_meaning: a person obsessed with getting rich quickly (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 「發財巴」是香港粵語俚語，用來形容那些熱衷於快速致富、追逐暴利或容易相信“速成致富”方案的人，常帶貶義。
explanation_english: “發財巴” is Hong Kong Cantonese slang for someone obsessed with getting rich quick — a person who chases fast profits or is prone to believing get-rich-quick schemes; often used pejoratively.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日諗住點快啲發財，真係個發財巴。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 seng4 jat6 nam2 zyu6 dim2 faai3 di1 faat3 coi4, zan1 hai6 go3 faat3 coi4 baa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他总是想着怎样快点发财，真是个想发财的人。
examples.english_sentence: He is always thinking about how to get rich fast — he's really someone obsessed with getting rich.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好信啲發財巴嘅投資騙局，好多都係陷阱。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 seon3 di1 faat3 coi4 baa1 ge3 tau4 zi1 pin3 guk6, hou2 do1 dou1 hai6 haam6 ging2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要相信那些想发财者的投资骗局，很多都是陷阱。
examples.english_sentence: Don't fall for those get-rich-quick investment scams — many of them are traps.

mandarin_meaning: 祝你發財並建立良好品格或名聲（恭賀語）
english_meaning: A colloquial Cantonese blessing meaning 'get rich and establish good character/reputation'; literally 'become wealthy and establish (one's) character/reputation'.
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語祝賀語或俗語，字面由「發財」和「立品」組成，用來祝願對方既能致富，又能有良好的品格、地位或名聲。有時帶玩笑或諷刺意味，視語境而定。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial blessing/idiom combining 'faat coi' (get rich) and 'laap ban' (establish character/reputation). It expresses a wish that someone will gain wealth and also establish good standing or character. Depending on context it can be earnest, playful, or slightly ironic.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 新年見面，大家會講「發財立品」，祝你有錢又有面子。
examples.jyutping_sentence: san1 nin4 gin3 min6, daai6 gaa1 wui5 gong2 'faat3 coi4 laap6 ban2', zuk1 nei5 jau5 cin2 jau6 jau5 min6 zi2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 新年見面，大家會說「發財立品」，祝你有錢又有面子。
examples.english_sentence: When we meet at Lunar New Year, people say '發財立品', wishing you both money and face/status.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語俚語）字面上是「發財的車」，指被認為能帶來財運或盈利的車輛；也可引申為比喻能帶來好運或賺錢機會的人或事物。
english_meaning: A Cantonese slang literally meaning "fortune car"; a vehicle believed to bring good luck or profit. By extension, something or someone thought to bring financial gain or luck.
explanation_mandarin: 「發財車」常在香港粵語口語中使用，既可指某部車被人視為能帶來好運或生意興隆，也可用作比喻，形容某個人、物或機會帶來財運或利潤。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese slang, "發財車" can refer to a vehicle that people jokingly or superstitiously believe brings good fortune or booming business. It is also used metaphorically for a person, object, or opportunity that brings profit or luck.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今朝喺街見到部發財車，結果成個月生意都順咗，真係唔知信唔信。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 ziu1 hai2 gaai1 gin3 dou3 bou6 faat3 coi4 ce1, git3 gwo2 sing4 go3 jyut6 sang1 ji3 dou1 seon6 zo2, zan1 hai6 m4 zi1 seon3 m4 seon3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天早上在街上看到一輛發財車，結果整個月生意都順利起來，真不知道該不該相信。
examples.english_sentence: This morning I saw a "fortune car" on the street; afterwards business went well for the whole month — I don't know whether to believe it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢買咗部二手車，大家都叫佢係發財車，覺得佢之後做生意好順。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 maai5 zo2 bou6 ji6 sau2 ce1, daai6 gaa1 dou1 giu3 keoi5 hai6 faat3 coi4 ce1, gok3 dak1 keoi5 zi1 hau6 zou6 saang1 ji3 hou2 seon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他買了一輛二手車，大家都稱那是發財車，覺得他之後做生意很順利。
examples.english_sentence: He bought a used car and everyone dubbed it a "fortune car", thinking his business would go well afterward.

mandarin_meaning: 发起（开始、发动或提出某项活动、倡议或计划）
english_meaning: to initiate; to launch; to start (an action, campaign, project, petition, etc.)
explanation_mandarin: 表示發動或提出一項活動、運動、計劃或倡議，通常是由個人或團體開始組織某事。
explanation_english: Used to indicate starting, launching, or proposing an activity, campaign, project, or initiative—usually organized or set in motion by a person or group.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個活動係我哋發起嘅。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 wut6 dung6 hai6 ngo5 dei6 faat3 hei2 ge3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个活动是我们发起的。
examples.english_sentence: This event was initiated by us.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢發起咗一個籌款運動，想幫助受災嘅家庭。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 faat3 hei2 zo2 jat1 go3 cau4 fun2 wan6 dung6, soeng2 bong1 zo6 sau6 zoi1 ge3 gaa1 ting4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他发起了一个筹款活动，想帮助受灾的家庭。
examples.english_sentence: He started a fundraising campaign to help families affected by the disaster.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 公司打算下個月發起新項目嘅試行計劃。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gung1 si1 daa2 syun3 haa6 go3 jyut6 faat3 hei2 san1 hong6 muk6 ge3 si3 hang4 gai3 waak6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 公司打算下个月发起新项目的试行计划。
examples.english_sentence: The company plans to launch a pilot program for the new project next month.

mandarin_meaning: 发迹；成名或发家致富、出人头地
english_meaning: to rise to prominence or make a fortune; to go from obscurity/poverty to wealth or higher status
explanation_mandarin: 指人从无到有、得到财富或社会地位的提升。常用于描述通过某种方式（如经商、投资、成名等）获得成功或发家。
explanation_english: Refers to someone rising from obscurity or poverty to gain wealth or status. Commonly used to describe becoming successful or making a fortune through business, investment, fame, etc.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢靠炒股票發跡，家陣好有錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 kaau3 caau2 gu2 piu3 faat3 zik6, gaa1 zan6 hou2 jau5 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他靠炒股票发迹，现在很有钱。
examples.english_sentence: He made his fortune by speculating in stocks; now he's very rich.

mandarin_meaning: （馬）揚蹄騰躍、迅速奔跑；比喻突然疾速離去
english_meaning: to rear and gallop (like a horse); to bolt or dash off quickly; can be used figuratively for someone suddenly rushing away
explanation_mandarin: 用來形容馬等動物揚起蹄子騰躍、迅速奔跑，也可用作比喻，表示人或事物突然急速離開或衝出。
explanation_english: Describes an animal (typically a horse) rearing its hooves and leaping or galloping away rapidly. Figuratively, it can mean someone or something suddenly dashing off or leaving in haste.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 聽到槍聲，馬群受驚即刻發蹄騰走。
examples.jyutping_sentence: teng1 dou3 coeng1 seng1, maa5 kwan4 sau6 ging1 zik1 haak1 faat3 tai4 tang4 zau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 聽到槍聲，馬群受驚立刻發蹄奔走。
examples.english_sentence: Hearing the gunfire, the herd of horses panicked and galloped off immediately.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 比賽一開始，馬匹就發蹄騰衝出去。
examples.jyutping_sentence: bei2 coi3 jat1 hoi1 ci2, maa5 pat1 zau6 faat3 tai4 tang4 cung1 ceot1 heoi3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 比賽一開始，馬匹就發蹄奔馳出去。
examples.english_sentence: As soon as the race started, the horses bolted and sped off.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）發瘋、發神經、失控、失去理性
english_meaning: Colloquial: to freak out, lose control, act irrationally
explanation_mandarin: 「發身」為香港粵語的口語用法，通常指突然行為失控、情緒激動或說話奇怪、失常。語氣偏非正式，可與「發神經」「發瘋」「發飆」相近。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to suddenly lose control, act irrationally, or 'freak out'. Informal usage, similar to 'go crazy', 'snap', or 'flip out'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日又開始發身，講嘢好離譜。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 jau6 hoi1 ci2 faat3 san1, gong2 je5 hou2 lei4 pou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天又開始發身，說話很離譜。
examples.english_sentence: He started acting up again today, saying ridiculous things.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我個仔最近成日發身，好易激動。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 go3 zai2 zeoi3 gan6 sing4 jat6 faat3 san1, hou2 ji6 gik1 dung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我家孩子最近經常發身，很容易激動。
examples.english_sentence: My kid has been freaking out a lot lately; he gets easily agitated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好亂鬧佢，佢都係有時會發身。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 lyun6 naau6 keoi5, keoi5 dou1 hai6 jau5 si4 wui5 faat3 san1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別亂罵他，他只是有時會發身。
examples.english_sentence: Don't scold him randomly; he just sometimes loses control.

mandarin_meaning: 发软（变得无力或软弱）
english_meaning: to go soft; become weak (physically or lose courage)
explanation_mandarin: 表示身體部位（如腿、手）感到無力、軟弱，或在情緒上失去勇氣、變得膽怯。
explanation_english: Describes becoming physically weak (muscles giving out) or emotionally losing nerve/courage — to go soft or feel weak.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 行咗成日，我條腿發軟，行唔穩。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haang4 zo2 seng4 jat6, ngo5 tiu4 teoi2 faat3 jyun5, haang4 m4 wan2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 走了一整天，我的腿发软，走得不稳。
examples.english_sentence: After walking all day, my legs went weak and I couldn't walk steadily.

mandarin_meaning: 臨陣退縮；膽怯，縮手縮腳
english_meaning: to chicken out; to lose one's nerve; to back out due to fear or timidity
explanation_mandarin: 口語、俚語說法，字面是「發（出）軟蹄」，用來形容人在關鍵時刻膽怯、退縮、不敢面對或參與某事。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang phrase literally meaning "to develop soft hooves." It describes someone getting cold feet or losing courage at a critical moment and backing out.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢到咗現場見到人咁多，就發軟蹄走咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dou3 zo2 jin6 coeng4 gin3 dou3 jan4 gam2 do1, zau6 faat3 jyun5 tai4 zau2 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他到場看到那麼多人，就臨陣退縮走了。
examples.english_sentence: He arrived at the venue, saw so many people, and chickened out and left.

mandarin_meaning: 负责办理；处理
english_meaning: to handle; to take care of; to arrange or make arrangements for something
explanation_mandarin: 在廣東話中，「發辦」表示負責安排或辦理某件事，常用於指派人去處理或籌辦某項事務。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "發辦" means to be responsible for arranging or handling something; often used to indicate assigning someone to deal with or organize a task or event.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事由我嚟發辦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 jau4 ngo5 lai4 faat3 baan6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這件事由我來負責辦理。
examples.english_sentence: I'll take care of this matter.

mandarin_meaning: 发送 (fāsòng)：寄出、传送（例如邮件、货物或讯息）
english_meaning: to send; to dispatch; to transmit (e.g., messages, parcels, data)
explanation_mandarin: 表示把物品或訊息從一方送到另一方，或將資料傳出給接收者。
explanation_english: Indicates sending or dispatching something (a message, parcel, data) from one party to another.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我已經發送咗嗰封電郵畀佢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 ji5 ging1 faat3 sung3 zo2 go2 fung1 din6 jau4 bei2 keoi5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我已经把那封电邮发送给他。
examples.english_sentence: I have already sent that email to him.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢哋會喺今日下午發送貨物。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 dei6 wui5 hai6 gam1 jat6 haa6 ng5 faat3 sung3 fo3 mat6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他们会在今天下午发送货物。
examples.english_sentence: They will dispatch the goods this afternoon.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 系統發送咗一個驗證碼去我嘅手機。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hai6 tung2 faat3 sung3 zo2 jat1 go3 jim6 zing3 maa5 heoi3 ngo5 ge3 sau2 gei1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 系统发送了一个验证码到我的手机。
examples.english_sentence: The system sent a verification code to my phone.

mandarin_meaning: （字面）發放或收到豬蹄；（俗語/方言用法）不常見，通常以字面意思使用，指在慶典或鄉村習俗中分發豬蹄作為食品或禮物。
english_meaning: Literally "have given/received pig's trotters." Not a common idiom — usually used literally to mean handing out or receiving pig's trotters (e.g., as food or a traditional gift at celebrations).
explanation_mandarin: 「發過豬蹄」在廣東話裡並非普遍成語或固定俚語，通常按字面理解，表示發出或收到豬蹄。這類用法多見於傳統節慶、喜慶或鄉村習俗中，把豬蹄當作食品或贈品分發給鄰里、親友或小孩。
explanation_english: “發過豬蹄” is not a widely used idiom in Cantonese; it is generally taken literally to mean having given or received pig's trotters. The expression appears in contexts of traditional celebrations or rural customs where pig's trotters are distributed as food or gifts to neighbors, guests, or children.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 上年阿婆生日，佢哋發過豬蹄俾街坊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng6 nin4 aa3 po4 sang1 jat6, keoi5 dei6 faat3 gwo3 zyu1 tai4 bei2 gaai1 fong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 去年奶奶生日，他們發了豬蹄給鄰居。
examples.english_sentence: Last year for grandma's birthday, they handed out pig's trotters to the neighbors.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢話細個時村裡會發過豬蹄畀細路仔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 waa6 sai3 go3 si4 cyun1 lei5 wui5 faat3 gwo3 zyu1 tai4 bei2 sai3 lou6 zai2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他說小時候村裡會發豬蹄給小孩子。
examples.english_sentence: He said when he was little the village would give pig's trotters to the children.

mandarin_meaning: 裝傻／當傻瓜（被人愚弄或做出愚蠢行為）
english_meaning: to act like a fool / to be made a fool of
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用語，帶有貶義，表示做出愚蠢的行為或被人當成傻瓜、上當受騙。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese slang phrase, derogatory in tone, meaning to behave foolishly or to be taken advantage of / made a fool of.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好發過豬頭啦，佢哋淨係想呃你錢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 faat3 gwo3 zyu1 tau4 laa1, keoi5 dei6 zing6 hai6 soeng2 aak1 nei5 cin2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別裝傻了，他們只是想騙你的錢。
examples.english_sentence: Don't act like a fool; they're just trying to scam your money.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 發過豬頭做咩？快啲講真話啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 gwo3 zyu1 tau4 zou6 me1? faai3 di1 gong2 zan1 waa6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 幹嘛裝傻？快點說實話吧。
examples.english_sentence: Why are you playing the fool? Tell the truth quickly.

mandarin_meaning: 发达 / 发财（指变得有钱、成功）
english_meaning: to get rich; to become prosperous/successful
explanation_mandarin: 粵語口語用詞，表示成為有錢或事業上成功。也可作祝福語或描述狀態。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb meaning to become wealthy or successful; can describe a state or be used as slang/expressions of wishing prosperity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢開公司幾年就發達喇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hoi1 gung1 si1 gei2 nin4 zau6 faat3 daat6 laa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他開公司幾年就發達了。
examples.english_sentence: He started a company and became rich after a few years.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 如果想發達，就要肯搏。
examples.jyutping_sentence: jyu4 gwo2 soeng2 faat3 daat6, zau6 jiu3 hang2 bok3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 如果想發達，就要肯拼搏。
examples.english_sentence: If you want to get rich or succeed, you have to be willing to work hard/take risks.

mandarin_meaning: 发还（把物品或款項歸還）
english_meaning: to return; to give back (an item, money, or rights) — often used in formal or legal contexts
explanation_mandarin: 表示把所佔有或被扣押的物品、款項或權利交還給原來的持有人或應得者，常用於正式或法律語境，例如法院、銀行或機構處理財物時會使用此詞。
explanation_english: Indicates returning possession of an item, funds, or rights to the original owner or rightful recipient. Commonly used in formal or legal contexts (e.g., courts, banks, institutions returning seized or incorrectly taken property).

examples.cantonese_sentence: 法院裁定將贓款發還畀受害人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faat3 jyun6 coi4 ding6 zoeng1 zong1 fun2 faat3 waan4 bei2 sau6 hoi6 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 法院裁定將贓款發還給受害人。
examples.english_sentence: The court ordered the confiscated funds to be returned to the victim.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 商店發還咗錯收嘅錢畀客人。
examples.jyutping_sentence: soeng1 dim3 faat3 waan4 zo2 co3 sau1 ge3 cin2 bei2 haak3 jan4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 商店已將多收的錢發還給客人。
examples.english_sentence: The store returned the money that was wrongly charged to the customer.

mandarin_meaning: 發配到邊疆；流放到偏遠邊境（多指懲罰性地流放或調派）
english_meaning: to exile/send someone to the frontier; to banish or assign to a remote border post (often as punishment)
explanation_mandarin: 指把人發往邊境或偏遠地區服役或流放，多見於古代用法；也可引申指把人邊緣化或放逐。
explanation_english: Refers to sending someone to serve or be exiled in frontier or remote areas, historically a form of punishment; can also be used figuratively to mean marginalizing or banishing someone.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢因為犯咗罪，被發配邊疆。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jan1wai6 faan6 zo2 zeoi6 bei6 faat3 pui3 bin1 goeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他因為犯罪，被發配到邊疆。
examples.english_sentence: He was exiled to the frontier for committing a crime.

mandarin_meaning: 喝酒後感到寒冷或發抖；因飲酒而著涼
english_meaning: to feel chills or shiver after drinking alcohol; to catch a chill because of drinking
explanation_mandarin: 俗語，指人在飲酒後因血管擴張或外界寒冷等原因而感到寒顫、發抖或容易著涼。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese phrase meaning someone feels chilled or starts shivering after drinking, often leading to catching a cold.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好喺凍風度飲太多酒，驚你會發酒寒。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 hai2 dung3 fung1 dou6 jam2 taai3 do1 zau2, ging1 nei5 wui5 faat3 zau2 hon4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要在有冷風的地方喝太多酒，怕你會發酒寒（喝完酒後著涼）。
examples.english_sentence: Don't drink too much out in the cold wind — you might get chilled from the alcohol.

mandarin_meaning: 发酵（fāxiào），指微生物作用使有機物質轉化；也可比喻事態逐步醞釀、擴大
english_meaning: fermentation; to ferment; (figuratively) to brew or to be brewing
explanation_mandarin: 指在酵母或細菌等微生物作用下，使食物或物質發生化學轉變（如酒、醬、泡菜等）；引申為事件、情緒等逐步醞釀、發展。
explanation_english: Refers to the biochemical process by which microorganisms (yeasts, bacteria) convert substances (e.g., in making wine, sauces, pickles); figuratively, it means a situation or sentiment gradually building up or brewing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啲泡菜係靠發酵先夠味。
examples.jyutping_sentence: di1 paau4coi3 hai6 kaau3 faat3 haau3 sin1 gau3 mei6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 泡菜要靠发酵才有味道。
examples.english_sentence: Pickles need fermentation to develop their flavor.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件事發酵咗一陣，宜家開始有好多討論。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 si6 faat3 haau3 zo2 jat1 zan6, ji4 gaa1 hoi1 ci2 jau5 hou2 do1 tou2 leon6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件事发酵了一阵子，现在开始有很多讨论。
examples.english_sentence: This matter has been brewing for a while; now there is a lot of discussion about it.

mandarin_meaning: 發行鈔票；比喻大量獲利或輕易賺大錢
english_meaning: to issue/print banknotes; (slang) to make a lot of money easily; to be a cash cow
explanation_mandarin: 本義指政府或中央銀行發行鈔票；口語上也用來比喻商業活動獲利豐厚、像是在「印錢」一樣。
explanation_english: Literally to issue or print banknotes; colloquially used to describe generating large profits or an activity/business that is making money easily.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 央行每隔幾年會發鈔，推出新版鈔票。
examples.jyutping_sentence: joeng1 hong4 mui5 gok3 gei2 nin4 wui5 faat3 caau1, teoi1 ceot1 san1 baan2 caau1 piu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 央行每隔幾年會發鈔，推出新版鈔票。
examples.english_sentence: The central bank issues banknotes every few years, releasing a new series of banknotes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢間店最近賣得好好，簡直係發鈔。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gaan1 dim3 zeoi3 gan6 maai6 dak1 hou2 hou2, gaan2 zik6 hai6 faat3 caau1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間店最近賣得很好，簡直是在發鈔。
examples.english_sentence: This shop has been selling so well recently, it's practically printing money.

mandarin_meaning: 發鈔銀行 / 發行銀行（有權發行紙幣的銀行）
english_meaning: note-issuing bank; bank authorized to issue banknotes
explanation_mandarin: 指在特定司法管轄區內，經政府或中央銀行授權可以發行紙幣（銀行鈔票）的銀行。例如香港現時有三間發鈔銀行，負責發行港元紙幣。
explanation_english: Refers to a bank that is authorized by the government or central monetary authority to issue banknotes in a given jurisdiction. For example, Hong Kong currently has three note-issuing banks that issue Hong Kong dollar banknotes.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 香港有三間發鈔銀行，可以發行港元紙幣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: hoeng1 gong2 jau5 saam1 gaan1 faat3 caau1 ngan4 hong4, ho2 ji5 faat3 hang4 gong2 jyun4 zi2 bai3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 香港有三家發鈔銀行，可以發行港元紙幣。
examples.english_sentence: Hong Kong has three note-issuing banks that can issue Hong Kong dollar banknotes.

mandarin_meaning: 炫耀花錢、用金錢顯擺以引人注目或令他人尷尬
english_meaning: to flaunt spending or hand out money ostentatiously to show off, often causing awkwardness or resentment
explanation_mandarin: 「發錢寒」是香港廣東話的口語用法，指透過花錢或派錢來炫耀或顯擺，讓別人感到尷尬或不舒服。常用於形容愛用金錢顯示身份或優越感的人。
explanation_english: A Hong Kong Cantonese colloquial expression meaning to flaunt money (spending or giving money) to show off or impress, often making others feel awkward, obliged, or resentful.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日發錢寒，好多人都唔鍾意同佢一齊出街。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 faat3 cin2 hon4, hou2 do1 jan4 dou1 m4 zung1 ji3 tung4 keoi5 jat1 cai4 ceot1 gaai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他總是炫耀花錢，很多人都不喜歡和他一起出門。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps flaunting his money; many people don't like going out with him.

mandarin_meaning: 開始胡說八道或做不切實際的幻想／吹牛
english_meaning: to start fantasizing or talking unrealistic/boastful nonsense
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，指某人開始說一些不切實際、浮誇或自以為是的話，像在做白日夢或吹牛。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang phrase meaning someone begins to say unrealistic, boastful, or delusional things — essentially daydreaming aloud or talking big.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日發開口夢，講到自己好有錢，其實一蚊都冇。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 faat3 hoi1 hau2 mung6, gong2 dou3 zi6 gei2 hou2 jau5 cin2, kei4 sat6 jat1 man1 dou1 mou5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他老是發開口夢，說自己很有錢，其實一塊錢都沒有。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps spouting fantasies, saying he's rich, but he doesn't even have a dollar.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好畀佢發開口夢，先把計劃做實啲。
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 bei2 keoi5 faat3 hoi1 hau2 mung6, sin1 baa2 gai3 waak6 zou6 sat6 di1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 不要讓他發開口夢，先把計劃做實一點。
examples.english_sentence: Don't let him daydream — make the plan more realistic first.

mandarin_meaning: 倒霉；運氣很差（俚語）
english_meaning: to be jinxed; to have a streak of bad luck (slang)
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，字面是「得了雞瘟」，常用來形容接連倒霉或運氣非常差，尤指在賭博、比賽或做事時屢屢失利。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression literally meaning "to get chicken plague." It describes being jinxed or experiencing a run of bad luck, especially in gambling, games, or repeated failures.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢頭先打牌打到發雞瘟，連輸咗三局。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 tau4 sin1 daa2 paai4 daa2 dou3 faat3 gai1 man1, lin4 syu1 zo2 saam1 guk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他剛才打牌倒霉，連輸了三局。
examples.english_sentence: He was really unlucky playing cards just now, losing three rounds in a row.

mandarin_meaning: （粵語俚語）失去理智、在賭博或興奮時衝動亂下注或亂花錢
english_meaning: Cantonese slang for losing control (especially when gambling or in a frenzy), impulsively betting or spending recklessly
explanation_mandarin: 「發雞盲」是粵語口語俚語，用來形容人在賭博、興奮或情緒失控時衝動行為──亂下注、亂花錢或不顧後果，通常會導致輸錢或後悔。
explanation_english: “Faat gai mong” is Cantonese slang describing someone who loses self-control (often in gambling or a frenzy), making impulsive bets or spending recklessly and usually suffering losses or regret.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一去賭場就發雞盲，成晚都唔識收手。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 heoi3 dou2 coeng4 zau6 faat3 gai1 mong4, seng4 maan5 dou1 m4 sik1 sau1 sau2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一去赌场就发鸡盲，整晚都不懂收手。
examples.english_sentence: Whenever he goes to the casino he goes 'faat gai mong' and can't stop all night.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 啱啱贏咗啲錢佢就發雞盲，結果輸返晒全部。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aam1 aam1 jing4 zo2 di1 cin2 keoi5 zau6 faat3 gai1 mong4, git3 gwo2 syu1 faan1 saai3 cyun4 bou6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 刚赢了些钱他就发鸡盲，结果把全部又输光了。
examples.english_sentence: He just won some money and then went 'faat gai mong', ending up losing it all.

mandarin_meaning: 发起攻击或挑衅；突然责难、找麻烦
english_meaning: to launch an attack or provoke; to pick a fight or suddenly criticize someone
explanation_mandarin: 「發難」用來表示開始攻擊、挑釁或突然對某人提出責難、找麻煩。可用於政治、社會衝突或人際衝突情境。
explanation_english: Used to indicate initiating an attack or provocation, or suddenly criticizing/picking a fight with someone. Applicable in political, social, or interpersonal conflict contexts.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老闆突然發難，責怪員工做得唔好。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 baan2 dat6 jin4 faat3 naan6, zaak3 gwaai3 jyun4 gung1 zou6 dak1 m4 hou2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老板突然发难，责怪员工做得不好。
examples.english_sentence: The boss suddenly picked a fight, blaming the employees for poor work.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢成日對啲新同事發難，令佢哋好唔舒服。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 sing4 jat6 deoi3 di1 san1 tung4 si6 faat3 naan6, ling6 keoi5 dei6 hou2 m4 syu1 fuk6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他经常对新同事发难，让他们很不舒服。
examples.english_sentence: He often picks on the new colleagues, making them feel very uncomfortable.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 示威者向警方發難，局勢一度緊張。
examples.jyutping_sentence: si6 wai1 ze2 hoeng3 ging2 fong4 faat3 naan6, guk6 si6 jat1 dou6 gan2 zoeng1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 示威者向警方发难，局势一度紧张。
examples.english_sentence: Protesters clashed with the police, and the situation became tense for a while.

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）性興奮；激起性慾
english_meaning: slang: to get sexually aroused; to be turned on
explanation_mandarin: 在香港粵語口語中，「發電」原意為發電，但作俚語時常用來形容看到某人或某事物而產生性興奮或欲望。
explanation_english: In Hong Kong Cantonese slang, literally 'generate electricity', but used to describe becoming sexually aroused or turned on by someone or something.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到啲性感相就發電。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 di1 sing3 gok3 soeng2 zau6 faat3 din6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到那些性感的照片就會起性慾。
examples.english_sentence: He gets turned on when he sees those sexy photos.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我唔知點解會對佢發電。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 m4 zi1 dim2 gaai2 wui5 deoi3 keoi5 faat3 din6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我不知道為什麼會對他產生性慾。
examples.english_sentence: I don't know why I get turned on by him.

mandarin_meaning: 发电厂
english_meaning: power plant; power station
explanation_mandarin: 指生產或供應電力的設施或建築物；在口語中有時也可比喻為提供能量或動力的個人或單位（如“部門的發電廠”意指非常有活力或生產力的人/團隊）。
explanation_english: Refers to a facility or building that generates and supplies electricity. In informal usage it can be used metaphorically to mean a person or unit that provides energy or drives productivity (e.g., 'the department's powerhouse').

examples.cantonese_sentence: 城市附近有一座大型發電廠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: sing4 si5 fu6 gan6 jau5 jat1 zo6 daai6 jing4 faat3 din6 cong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 城市附近有一座大型发电厂。
examples.english_sentence: There is a large power plant near the city.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 阿明做嘢好有動力，係我哋部門嘅發電廠。
examples.jyutping_sentence: aa3 ming4 zou6 je5 hou2 jau5 dung6 lik6, hai6 ngo5 dei6 bou6 mun4 ge3 faat3 din6 cong2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 阿明工作很有动力，是我们部门的“发电厂”。
examples.english_sentence: Ah Ming is very energetic at work; he's the 'powerhouse' of our department.

mandarin_meaning: 发电机
english_meaning: generator (electrical device); (figuratively) someone or something that generates energy or drives others
explanation_mandarin: 指把其他形式的能量（如机械能、化学能）转换为电能的机器。口语中也可比喻某人或事物不断提供动力或能量。
explanation_english: Refers to a machine that converts other forms of energy (e.g. mechanical, chemical) into electricity. Colloquially, it can be used metaphorically for a person or thing that continuously provides energy or drives others.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 屋企突然停電，夜晚要用發電機先有電。
examples.jyutping_sentence: uk1 kei2 dak6 syun4 ting4 din6, je6 maan5 jiu3 jung6 faat3 din6 gei1 sin1 jau5 din6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 家裡突然停电，晚上要用发电机才有电。
examples.english_sentence: The power at home went out suddenly; we need to use a generator tonight to have electricity.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺團隊入面好似一部發電機，一直帶動大家向前衝。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai6 tyun4 deoi2 jap6 min6 hou2 ci5 jat1 bou6 faat3 din6 gei1, jat1 zik6 daai3 dung6 daai6 gaa1 hoeng3 cin4 cung1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在团队里像一台发电机，一直带动大家向前冲。
examples.english_sentence: He is like a generator in the team, constantly driving everyone forward.

mandarin_meaning: 發霉
english_meaning: to become moldy; to mildew; (figuratively) to become stale or neglected
explanation_mandarin: 指因潮濕或不潔而長出霉菌，物品表面出現毛狀或斑點；也可比喻某事物因被忽視或長期未更新而變得過時或退化。
explanation_english: Refers to the growth of mold on items due to dampness or poor hygiene, producing fuzzy or spotted patches; can also be used figuratively to describe something becoming stale, neglected, or outdated.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢塊麵包發霉咗，唔好食啦。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 faai3 min6 baau1 faat3 mui4 zo2, m4 hou2 sik6 laa1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這塊麵包發霉了，別吃了。
examples.english_sentence: This piece of bread has gone moldy; don't eat it.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 衣櫃入面因為潮濕，件衫開始發霉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ji1 gwai6 jap6 min6 jan1 wai6 ciu4 sap1, gin6 saam1 hoi1 ci2 faat3 mui4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 衣櫃因為潮濕，衣服開始發霉。
examples.english_sentence: Because the wardrobe was damp, the clothes started to mildew.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 間公司啲制度冇更新，聽落有啲發霉。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gaan1 gung1si1 di1 zai3 dou6 mou5 gang1 san1, teng1 lok6 jau5 di1 faat3 mui4.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 這間公司的制度沒有更新，感覺有點過時。
examples.english_sentence: This company's rules haven't been updated; they feel a bit stale/outdated.

mandarin_meaning: 露出羨慕或嫉妒的表情（眼睛像發出青色光芒）
english_meaning: to show envy/jealousy; eyes light up with desire or greed
explanation_mandarin: 口語說法，形容看到別人有好東西或想要的東西時，露出羨慕或貪婪的表情，像眼睛發出青光。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression describing the look of envy or greedy desire someone shows when they see something they want — as if their eyes emit a greenish light.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到我張新手袋即刻發青光。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 ngo5 zoeng1 san1 sau2 doi2 zik1 haak1 faat3 ceng1 gwong1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到我的新手袋立刻露出羨慕的表情。
examples.english_sentence: He saw my new handbag and immediately looked envious.

mandarin_meaning: 发音 (fāyīn) — 发出或读出语言的音；词语的读法
english_meaning: pronunciation; to pronounce
explanation_mandarin: 指字詞或語音的發聲方式和讀法；可作名詞表示“發音”，亦可作動詞表示“發出聲音/念出來”。
explanation_english: Refers to the way sounds or words are produced and read aloud; can be used as a noun meaning 'pronunciation' or as a verb meaning 'to pronounce'.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢個字嘅發音係點？
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 go3 zi6 ge3 faat3 jam1 hai6 dim2?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这个字的发音是什么？
examples.english_sentence: What's the pronunciation of this character?

examples.cantonese_sentence: 老師教我哋正確嘅發音。
examples.jyutping_sentence: lou5 si1 gaau3 ngo5 dei6 zing3 kok3 ge3 faat3 jam1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 老师教我们正确的发音。
examples.english_sentence: The teacher teaches us the correct pronunciation.

mandarin_meaning: （口語）發瘋、失去理智或情緒失控；也可指因興奮或迷戀而衝動行事
english_meaning: Colloquial: to go crazy or lose control (emotionally or behaviorally); can also mean getting overly excited or acting impulsively (sometimes from infatuation).
explanation_mandarin: 廣東話口語，形容一個人因情緒、興奮或衝動而表現失常、做出怪異或誇張的行為；有時帶調侃或誇張語氣。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial verb describing someone acting irrationally or wildly due to emotion, excitement, or impulse; often used jokingly or hyperbolically.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢見到鍾意嗰個女仔就發風，樣樣都唔理。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gin3 dou3 zung1 ji3 go2 go3 neoi5 zai2 zau6 faat3 fung1, joeng6 joeng6 dou1 m4 lei5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他看到喜歡的女孩就發瘋，什麼都不管。
examples.english_sentence: He goes crazy when he sees the girl he likes; he ignores everything.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 考完試啲學生發風，成晚都開派對。
examples.jyutping_sentence: haau2 jyun4 si3 di1 hok6 sang1 faat3 fung1, sing4 maan5 dou1 hoi1 paai3 deoi6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 考試一結束學生就瘋狂興奮，整晚都在開派對。
examples.english_sentence: After exams the students get hyped and party all night.

mandarin_meaning: 出風頭、在公開場合（或社交媒體）張揚炫耀以吸引注意；有時帶有魯莽或誇張的行為
english_meaning: to show off ostentatiously (often publicly or on social media); to seek attention by being flashy or making a scene; sometimes implies reckless or exaggerated behavior
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俗語，指在公眾場合或網上誇張地展示自己、炫耀或搶風頭，有時也帶有魯莽或故意吸引別人注意的意味。
explanation_english: A Cantonese colloquial/slang expression meaning to ostentatiously show off or seek attention (often in public or online). It can carry a connotation of being flashy, attention-seeking, or even a bit reckless.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢喺Facebook成日發風發出面，成日炫耀新車。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 hai2 Facebook sing4 jat6 faat3 fung1 faat3 ceot1 min6, sing4 jat6 hyun3 jiu6 san1 ce1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他在Facebook上老是發風發出面，老是炫耀新車。
examples.english_sentence: He keeps showing off on Facebook, always bragging about his new car.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 唔好成日發風發出面，做嘢低調啲得唔得？
examples.jyutping_sentence: m4 hou2 sing4 jat6 faat3 fung1 faat3 ceot1 min6, zou6 je5 dai1 diu6 di1 dak1 m4 dak1?
examples.mandarin_sentence: 別老是發風發出面，做事低調一點可以嗎？
examples.english_sentence: Stop constantly showing off — can you be a bit more low-key in your actions?

mandarin_meaning: （俚語）突然性欲高涨；变得很色
english_meaning: (slanged) to suddenly become sexually aroused; to get horny
explanation_mandarin: 「發鷄瘟」是粵語粗俗俚語，字面意為「得了雞瘟」，實際用來形容某人突然性慾高漲或變得很色。多用於口語及非正式場合，帶有玩笑或貶義成分。
explanation_english: “發鷄瘟” is a Cantonese vulgar slang phrase literally meaning “catching the chicken plague.” It describes someone suddenly becoming very sexually aroused or horny. It’s colloquial and can be crude or joking.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢一見到靚女就發鷄瘟。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 jat1 gin3 dou2 leng3 neoi5 zau6 faat3 gai1 man1
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他一看到漂亮的女生就性欲高涨。
examples.english_sentence: He gets horny whenever he sees a pretty woman.

mandarin_meaning: 不常見的粵語俚語，可能為粗俗用語，確切含義不詳或地區性用法，字面可拆為「發」（變得）、「鷄」（俗稱，常見於粗口）和「盲」（盲目、糊塗）。
english_meaning: An obscure/rare Cantonese slang (likely vulgar). Exact meaning is unclear or regionally specific; literally can be parsed as 'faat (become) + gai (slang term often vulgar) + maang (blind)'.
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 俚語 / 粗口（非正式用語）
explanation_mandarin: 「發鷄盲*」屬於非正式粵語俚語或粗口詞彙，使用情況稀少且缺乏權威詞典記載。詞組可能由數個字組合而成，暗含粗俗意味；由於語義不明且可能具有冒犯性，建議避免在正式場合使用。如需了解具體用法，應諮詢使用該表達的語境來源或當地說話者。
explanation_english: “發鷄盲*” is an informal Cantonese slang/vulgar expression that is rare and not well documented. The phrase appears to combine elements that suggest a coarse meaning; because its precise usage and sense are unclear and potentially offensive, avoid using it in formal contexts. For exact understanding, consult speakers familiar with the specific regional usage or context where it appears.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好亂講「發鷄盲*」，呢啲粗口唔好亂用。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 lyun6 gong2 "faat3 gai1 maang4*", ni1 di1 cou1 hau2 m4 hou2 lyun6 jung6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要亂說「發鷄盲*」，這些粗口不要亂用。
examples.english_sentence: Don't casually say '發鷄盲*'—these vulgar terms shouldn't be used lightly.

mandarin_meaning: （動/形）變黑、發暗；（引申）臉色陰沉、變得不悅或生氣（如「面色發黑」）
english_meaning: to turn black or darken; to become discolored or blackened; (figuratively) to have a dark/sullen facial expression or become sullen/angry
explanation_mandarin: 「發黑」在粵語中可用來描述顏色變深或變黑（例如食物、皮膚或物件變色），也常用於描述人的臉色變差、看起來陰沉或生氣（如「面色發黑」）。視上下文可為動詞或形容詞。
explanation_english: In Cantonese, "發黑" describes something becoming dark or blackened (e.g., food, skin, objects). It can also be used figuratively to describe a person's face becoming dark or sullen (e.g., "face went dark"). Depending on context it functions as a verb or adjective.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 個蘋果唔新鮮，切開就發黑咗。
examples.jyutping_sentence: go3 ping4 gwo2 m4 san1 sin3, cit3 hoi1 zau6 faat3 hak1 zo2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那個蘋果不新鮮，切開就變黑了。
examples.english_sentence: The apple isn't fresh; it turned black when I cut it open.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢聽完嗰件事即刻面色發黑，唔想講嘢。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 teng1 jyun4 go2 gin6 si6 zik1 hak1 min6 sik1 faat3 hak1, m4 soeng2 gong2 je5.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他聽完那件事立刻臉色發黑，不想說話。
examples.english_sentence: After hearing that, his face went dark immediately; he didn't want to speak.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 塊牛扒放咗幾日，表面開始發黑，唔可以食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: faai3 ngau4 paa4 fong3 zo2 gei2 jat6, biu2 min6 hoi1 ci2 faat3 hak1, m4 ho2 ji5 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 那塊牛排放了幾天，表面開始變黑，不能吃。
examples.english_sentence: The steak sat for a few days; the surface started to turn black, it's not safe to eat.

mandarin_meaning: 发疯、发癫，行为失常或情绪失控
english_meaning: to go crazy; to act crazy or unhinged; to freak out
explanation_mandarin: 粵語俚語，表示突然情緒或行為失常、發瘋或做出誇張、失控的舉動。
explanation_english: A Cantonese slang expression meaning to suddenly lose control, act crazily or behave in an exaggerated/unhinged way.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 佢今日發𤷪𤺧，成日喺街度大聲喊。
examples.jyutping_sentence: keoi5 gam1 jat6 faat3 din1 din1, seng4 jat6 hai2 gaai1 dou6 daai6 sing1 haam3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 他今天發瘋，一直在街上大聲喊。
examples.english_sentence: He went crazy today, shouting loudly on the street all the time.

mandarin_meaning: 白 / 白色；白费；免费（视语境而定）
english_meaning: white (color); in vain / wasted; free of charge (depends on context)
partOfSpeech_mandarin: 形容詞 / 名詞 / 動詞（視語境而定）
explanation_mandarin: 「白」主要表示顏色（白色），也可用於詞語中表示徒然、白費或免費等意思。具體詞性和含義視上下文變化。
explanation_english: “白” primarily denotes the color white. In different contexts it can also mean 'in vain' or 'free of charge'. Part of speech and exact meaning depend on context.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 呢件衫係白色㗎。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ni1 gin6 saam1 hai6 baak6 sik1 gaa3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 这件衣服是白色的。
examples.english_sentence: This shirt is white.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你咁做係白費力氣。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 gam2 zou6 hai6 baak6 fai3 lik6 hei3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你这样做是在白费力气。
examples.english_sentence: What you're doing is wasting your effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 今日公司請客，我哋可以白食。
examples.jyutping_sentence: gam1 jat6 gung1 si1 cing2 haak3, ngo5 dei6 ho2 ji5 baak6 sik6.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 今天公司请客，我们可以免费吃。
examples.english_sentence: The company is treating today, we can eat for free.

mandarin_meaning: 白來一趟 / 徒勞無功
english_meaning: to come for nothing; a wasted trip; in vain
explanation_mandarin: 用來表示特地前往或付出努力最後卻徒勞無功、白費力氣。多見於粵語口語或帶粗俗色彩的說法，相當於「白來一趟」、「白費」。
explanation_english: Used to express that a trip or effort was wasted or ended up in vain. It is a colloquial/slang Cantonese expression (sometimes coarse) meaning a wasted trip or wasted effort.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我專登坐車嚟，佢話今日唔喺，真係白嚟死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 zyun1 dang1 co5 ce1 lai4, keoi5 waa6 gam1 jat6 m4 hai2, zan1 hai6 baak6 lai4 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我特意坐車來，他說今天不在，真是白來一趟。
examples.english_sentence: I purposely took the bus here and he said he's not here today — what a wasted trip.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 出發前打個電話先啦，唔好白嚟死。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ceot1 faat3 cin4 daa2 go3 din6 waa2 sin1 laa1, m4 hou2 baak6 lai4 sei2.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 出發前先打個電話吧，不要白來一趟。
examples.english_sentence: Call before you set off — don't come here for nothing.

mandarin_meaning: 白白浪費 / 白費力氣
english_meaning: a complete waste; wasted for nothing
explanation_mandarin: 口語俗語（常見於香港粵語），表示某事白白浪費，徒勞無功。可寫作「白嘥嘥」或簡稱「白嘥」。用來強調時間、心力或資源被浪費掉。
explanation_english: A colloquial Cantonese expression (common in Hong Kong) meaning that something was completely wasted or done in vain. Often written as "白嘥嘥" or shortened to "白嘥"; used to emphasize wasted time, effort, or resources.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我哋嗰次活動搞得咁差，啲時間同心機全部白嘥嘥。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 dei6 go2 ci3 wut6 dung6 gaau2 dak1 gam2 caa1, di1 si4 gaan3 tung4 sam1 gei1 cyun4 bou6 baak6 saai1 saai1.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我们那次活动办得那么糟，时间和心力全都白白浪费了。
examples.english_sentence: Our event that time was so poorly organized — all the time and effort were totally wasted.

mandarin_meaning: 白白地 / 白費 / 免費
english_meaning: for nothing; in vain; free of charge
explanation_mandarin: 口語用法，表示徒然、白費（做某事沒有結果）或表示免費、不用付錢。
explanation_english: Colloquial Cantonese adverb meaning 'in vain' or 'for nothing'; can also indicate something is given free of charge.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 你唔好白白浪費時間。
examples.jyutping_sentence: nei5 m4 hou2 baak6 baak6 long6 fai3 si4 gaan3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 你不要白白浪费时间。
examples.english_sentence: Don't waste time for nothing.

examples.cantonese_sentence: 我喺活動度白白攞咗張門票。
examples.jyutping_sentence: ngo5 hai2 wut6 dung6 dou6 baak6 baak6 lo2 zo2 zoeng1 mun4 piu3.
examples.mandarin_sentence: 我在活动上白白拿到了一张门票。
examples.english_sentence: I got a ticket for free at the event.

mandarin_meaning: 喪事；與喪禮、葬禮有關的事務
english_meaning: funeral; matters related to a death or funeral
explanation_mandarin: 「白事」是粵語常用詞，指與死亡後的喪葬、喪禮及相關事務有關的事情，相當於普通話的「喪事／喪禮」。
